reviewer.role: AI-assisted internal security reviewer working with the project owner

reviewDomains.summary: Strict parsing, canonical encodings, domain-separated signing inputs, replay/freshness bounds and exact operation binding remain fail-closed on the frozen target.

Critical protocol messages remain bound to both Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 verification with explicit key purpose, issuer, Node and fingerprint binding; no classical-only critical-message fallback was found.
evidence: v5 reviewer bundle hybrid signature sources/tests
KVM activation transport policy requires Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 critical signatures

reviewDomains.summary: TLS 1.3 plus X25519MLKEM768 remains mandatory and the prior LOW-001 ingress finding is remediated: verified client identity is now required at the TLS layer with ssl_verify_client on.
Signer UDS peer-credential checks, key-ID pinning and least-privilege read-only database access remain the enforced custody boundary.
evidence: v5 reviewer bundle signer sources and PostgreSQL role policy
prior AI-assisted audit isolated signer review

reviewDomains.summary: Replay nonce, prepared-key installation, epoch CAS, immutable ACK evidence and receipt binding remain transactionally coupled and fail closed.
evidence: v5 reviewer bundle PostgreSQL migrations and ACK/receipt implementation

reviewDomains.summary: The prior LOW-002 finding is remediated on the frozen Node target: master-key creation fsyncs the file and then the parent directory before reporting success; rotation/rollback durability ordering remains monotonic and fail-closed.

Coordinated restore and off-host recovery-floor logic are fail-closed and the live off-host witness passed; provider-managed storage remains an explicitly accepted external durability trust boundary rather than a physical-power qualification claim.
Retirement remains owner-authorized, checkpoint-bound and anti-resurrection protected; active identity and monotonic floor are preserved.
evidence: v5 reviewer bundle retirement protocol and tests
prior AI-assisted audit owner-authorized retirement review

reviewDomains.summary: Parser fuzz invariants and external compatible ML-DSA-65 verification vectors provide meaningful negative evidence; coverage remains bounded and is not represented as formal verification or certification.
evidence: v5 reviewer bundle parser fuzz targets
v5 reviewer bundle external ML-DSA-65 vector tests

reviewDomains.summary: Node and Nexus observability remain staging-gated, read-only and redacted; production activation and strict-PQ state remain false in observability outputs before execution.

The KVM activation policy requires exact candidate/evidence hashes, final canary and reviewed rollout evidence, fixes TLS 1.3/X25519MLKEM768/ML-DSA-65, forbids automatic or classical-only fallback, retains XMESH1 for separate retirement, and requires a separate execution step. External independent review is intentionally replaced by this AI-assisted internal review plus explicit release-owner risk acceptance.

findings.title: KVM provider durability remains an external trust boundary
findings.disposition: Release owner accepts reliance on provider-managed block storage durable-flush semantics for the KVM deployment class; this does not claim physical host/controller/PLP qualification.

findings.title: Assurance model is AI-assisted internal review rather than an independent third-party audit
findings.disposition: The release owner explicitly accepts the reduced organizational-independence assurance in exchange for a complete review of all mandatory domains and retained fail-closed technical gates.

signoff.statement: AI-assisted internal review of the exact v5 KVM frozen target found no unresolved Critical, High, Medium or Low release-blocking vulnerability. The two Low findings from the earlier internal audit are remediated in the current frozen target. Remaining items are documented informational/accepted-risk boundaries.

releaseOwnerRiskAcceptance.statement: Release owner explicitly replaces the mandatory independent external security-review requirement with an AI-assisted internal review plus owner risk acceptance because an external specialist is not currently practical. The owner accepts the reduced organizational-independence assurance. This does not waive the exact-candidate canary, rollout/rollback review, KVM durability evidence, provider-storage acceptance, bounded activation approval, or separate execution requirement, and it does not claim physical power-loss qualification.
